title: haruspex.json
description: The haruspex config file: which procedures are typed, per schema; overrides of what inference found; naming rules and emitter settings. Paths in it are relative to the file. JSON with comments and trailing commas is allowed.

source.description: The folder of .sql files to read, including subfolders; a database project's .sqlproj, read as its build reads it; or a .dacpac, read with the packages of its database it refers to. Relative to this file. The command line's source argument overrides it.

references.description: Folders to look for the DACPACs a .dacpac or .sqlproj source refers to, relative to this file, in order: after the folder of the package that refers to them, or where a project's build takes them from.

collation.description: The database's default collation, which a column without COLLATE takes, for a source that doesn't record it: a folder of .sql files. A .dacpac records its own and a .sqlproj gives its own, which wins. Without either, a value set of such a column is a comment, not an enum.

out.description: The folder to write haruspex.ir.json and haruspex.zod.ts to. --out overrides it.

schemas.description: Settings per schema, keyed by the schema's name exactly as in the database (no brackets; dots allowed). Nothing is selected unless its schema has a block with include. A key that names no schema of the project is an error.

objects.description: How result objects treat keys their type doesn't list. "strip" (the default) removes them when parsing (z.object), so a column the database adds before the application redeploys doesn't break it. "strict" fails on them (z.strictObject), for applications that deploy first or together with the database.

check.description: What haruspex check does beyond comparing the module with what is committed.

unknowns.description: "report" (the default): each unknown in the module is a note, and the check passes with them. "fail": any unknown fails the check, for a module that must be typed throughout.

session.description: The SET options the callers' connections set: the driver's at login, or what the application sets after. Each is true for ON or false for OFF; leave out one that isn't known, which claims only what holds whatever it is. A database's defaults apply only to a connection that sets nothing, and current drivers set these at login, so declare the driver's, not the database's.

ansiWarnings.description: ANSI_WARNINGS. On, an overflow or a division by zero is an error, not NULL, so it no longer makes a value nullable.

arithAbort.description: ARITHABORT. On, an overflow or a division by zero is an error, not NULL, as with ansiWarnings on.

concatNullYieldsNull.description: CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL. Off, string + with one side NULL gives the other side, so it is null only when both sides may be.

numericRoundAbort.description: NUMERIC_ROUNDABORT. Off, a decimal rounded to fewer places is rounded silently, so precision-loss no longer makes a value nullable; on, the rounding is an error, NULL only when ansiWarnings and arithAbort are both off, and NULL under TRY_CAST.

procedures.description: Overrides per procedure, keyed by its two-part name (schema.name, with T-SQL brackets around a part that holds a dot). name and paths need a selected procedure; results alone may be declared for any procedure, in the project or not.

propertyNames.description: A two-part name, without * or ? outside brackets: an override names one procedure.

name.description: The procedure's generated name, instead of the naming rules'.

paths.description: Overrides of places in the procedure's results, keyed by path: "lines[].sku", "[].status", "settings<json>.mode", or "results[1][].id" when it returns several result sets.

results.description: The procedure's result sets, declared where haruspex can't infer them (dynamic SQL, a system procedure, one outside the project): "none", one result, or an array of them in order. A call of the procedure contributes them to its caller. Needs why. Still checked at runtime.

why.description: Why the declared results hold. Required with results.

name.description: The name of the object type at the path.

nullable.description: false declares the value never null, which the database doesn't prove. Still checked at runtime.

why.description: Why the claim holds. Required with nullable and values.

type.description: An exported schema to use for the value, with [] for each level of array, such as "TagSchema[]".

import.description: The module that exports type: a package or alias such as "@app/types", or a path relative to this file.

values.description: "exact" declares that a value set the database compares under its collation holds exactly its items, giving z.enum. Still checked at runtime.

naming.description: How generated names are made from objects' own names (never their schemas), applied in order: replace, then the schema's prefix, then case. A schema's own naming merges over this one.

replace.description: Regular expressions replaced in the object's name, in order, such as { "pattern": "#$", "with": "Row" }. A schema's own rules run after the top-level ones.

pattern.description: A .NET regular expression without backreferences or lookarounds.

with.description: The replacement; $1 names a group. "" removes the match.

case.description: "pascal" (the default): GetOrder, with $, # and _ as word breaks. "camel": getOrder. "preserve": the name as it is, which must then be a valid identifier. A schema's own case replaces the top-level one.

include.description: The schema's procedures to type, by their own names: "get_order", "list_*", "*". * and ? match any characters and one character; brackets make what they hold literal; matching ignores case. A pattern that matches nothing is an error. --include (schema.pattern) overrides the file's includes for one run.

exclude.description: Procedures to leave out of those include selects, by their own names. Exclude wins over include. A pattern that excludes nothing is an error.

prefix.description: Put in front of the generated names of the schema's objects, before the case rules: "Audit" makes audit.get_order AuditGetOrder. Empty by default: names leave the schema out, and a clash between schemas is an error that a prefix resolves.

naming.description: Naming for this schema, merged over the top-level naming: its case replaces the top-level case, and its replace rules run after the top-level ones.

result.description: One declared result set: rowset, the JSON Schema of one row; or json, the JSON Schema of the document FOR JSON writes. Either is a schema, or the path of a file holding one, relative to this file.

rowset.description: The JSON Schema of one row: an object with properties, one per column, each a scalar.

json.description: The JSON Schema of the document the result holds.

mayBeAbsent.description: true when the JSON result may not be there: FOR JSON over no rows returns no row at all.

declaredSchema.description: A JSON Schema (type, properties, required, items, minItems, maxItems, additionalProperties, format and $ref to $defs are read), or the path of a file holding one.
